column1: # Claims this project has written down, proven false, and must not assert again.
# 🔴 WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. An independent review found that corrections here
# propagate to CLAUDE.md and stop: SECURITY.md was still telling security
# researchers that unslist.c is unreachable dead code -- the THIRD writing of a
# claim already disproven twice -- and "the settings file sits beside the
# executable" survived in four places while ADR 0007 recorded it as fixed.
# fork.h has five mechanical guards making it the single definition of the build
# tag (ADR 0006). Facts had none. verify-docs.ps1 is that guard, and this is its
# data.
# ⚠ A RETIRED CLAIM IS NOT A BANNED PHRASE, and getting that wrong makes the
# check useless. Three kinds of mention are legitimate and must not fire:
#   1. A NEGATION -- "the file is in the working directory, NOT beside the
#      executable" is the correction, not the error.
#   2. A QUOTATION -- FORK.md and tworld.c both write "beside the executable" in
#      quotes while explaining why it is wrong.
#   3. THE SAME WORDS MEANING SOMETHING ELSE -- ADR 0001 says the two DLLs "must
#      ship beside the executable", which is about zlib1.dll and is TRUE.
# So each row carries exemptions. Write them as tightly as the claim needs and
# no tighter: an exemption that swallows the assertion turns this row into
# decoration.
# COLUMNS, tab-separated:
#   id       short name, for the failure message
#   pattern  .NET regex; a line matching it is asserting the retired claim
#   exempt   .NET regex; if the SAME LINE also matches this, the mention is
#            legitimate. Use (?!) for "no exemptions".
#   why      what is actually true, printed when the check fires
